text:
Mike Babcock came out of retirement in June to replace Kris Knoblauch, and he put Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl on the same line from the first day of camp. Twenty games in, the Oilers are 14-3-3, McDavid is the runaway Hart favourite in Oilers Nation's awards poll, Evan Bouchard leads the Norris voting there, and more than one headline asks whether Devon Levi is the goalie Edmonton has been searching for.

Our numbers add a caution. Edmonton has scored about 20.8 more goals than its chances deserved, and it has only 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five. The three-game winning streak came with 47% of the chances. A lot of the scoring is concentrated in two places: the McDavid and Draisaitl line with Vasily Podkolzin, which has outscored opponents 20-6 with 62% of the chances, and the Mattias Ekholm and Bouchard pair, 21-4. When those groups sit, things look different; the line of Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels has 31% of the chances and is 5-10.

The goaltending has been steady rather than spectacular overall, but Tristan Jarry is on a run: a .942 save percentage and 5.9 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

Our numbers project about 106 points and give Edmonton a 97% chance at the playoffs. The cushion is real. What to watch is whether the depth chances improve before the finishing cools.
